server.name: openwork-den-api-agent
server.title: OpenWork Connect
server.description: Discover and use your organization's authorized connections, skills, and Workflows; build Apps and delegate work to OpenWork sessions.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Read openwork://agent/guidance.md with resources/read before working; it contains the full connection, remote-session, import, and Workflow rules.
Search capabilities with 2-4 keyword variants; execute only exact returned names. Copy external argumentsSchema into body and schemaDigest into schemaDigest. Schema guidance is advisory; never repeat a successful provider call because of it.
Only use intent connect for an explicit connect/reconnect request. Discovery must not trigger sign-in. Relay the connection's exact action; a downstream failure does not mean OpenWork needs reconnecting. Never invent credentials or claim setup is ready.
Use list_skills/get_skill for authorized skills and follow the matching skill before creating or sharing one. update_skill publishes an immutable version.
For Apps read build-an-app with get_skill, then use prepare_app/create_app/read_app/update_app; never substitute local HTML or legacy views. Open Apps via their discovered capability.
Honor requests to work remotely by delegating the whole request with remote-session:create/send, then reading its receipt; do not perform that work here. Only schedule an Automation when asked.

tool.name: create_app
tool.title: Create an App
tool.description: Create and publish an App as its own MCP server from complete React/CSS source, textFallback, and declared tools. Read skill:build-an-app for required source, host, approval, caching, and tool-call rules before writing source; start with prepare_app and pass its preparationId (optional for older clients). This call rechecks bindings, compiles source, and saves the App; no Workflow, output schema, or Automation is required. Bind exact capabilities from search_capabilities: saved Workflows, connection tools, or read-only OpenWork GET actions. To change OpenWork data, bind a saved Workflow. Tools run as the person using the App. Load read-only data on open after the launch result arrives; changes and approval-required calls need their own button, one call per click. Creates a new private Plugin unless pluginId selects an existing one. Bound Workflows join that Plugin; sharing it shares the App and those Workflows. Requires mcp:write. Returns app (summary including appId, pluginId, revisionId and tools, not source), input (empty launch input), mcpUrl, and usually launch { connectionId, toolName, resourceUri, arguments }. launch is omitted when the App is beyond OpenWork's connection limit; mcpUrl still works in MCP clients. OpenWork opens an available App in a sidebar tab; other hosts receive its MCP URL and text fallback. Reply briefly.

tool.name: update_app
tool.title: Update an App
tool.description: Update an existing App with complete replacement React source, title, and textFallback, following create_app's rules. First read_app, and copy its app.revisionId to expectedRevisionId. Omit cssSource, description, or tools to keep the current ones, or pass complete replacements. Follow skill:build-an-app's source and tool-call rules. Publishes an immutable revision in the same Plugin and MCP server; newly bound Workflows join that Plugin, so everyone it is shared with can run them. Requires editor access and the mcp:write scope. Returns app (updated summary, not source), input (empty launch input), mcpUrl, and launch { connectionId, toolName, resourceUri, arguments } unless OpenWork's connection limit prevents opening it. The MCP URL remains usable. OpenWork opens an available App in a sidebar tab.

tool.name: search_capabilities
tool.title: Search capabilities
tool.description: Search connection actions, saved Workflows, and skills by keyword. Direct tools such as create_skill, get_skill, and the App builders prepare_app, create_app, read_app, and update_app are outside this search; call them directly. Search covers native Google Workspace capabilities (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Gmail drafts), org-connected external MCPs, and namespaced OpenWork Admin tools for allowlisted platform admins. Accessible Workflows appear as marketplace matches with kind workflow and execute through execute_capability like every other exact search result. Try 2-4 keyword variants before deciding a capability is unavailable. Native API matches include a connector-namespaced name, pathParams, queryParams, querySchema, hasBody, and bodySchema. External MCP matches include argumentsSchema, schemaDigest, and invocation.argumentsField. A match with kind mcp_app is a standard MCP App launch capability, either an App built in OpenWork (its own MCP server at the match path) or an App from a connected MCP server; execute it normally and the OpenWork host will render its advertised ui:// resource. Returns matches with exact name, summary, kind, invocation schemas, and connection status where available; optional hint explains coverage or next steps. connectionAction carries an explicit sign-in card; connectorCatalog contains setup suggestions, not executable tools. Built-in and marketplace skills return SKILL.md when executed; list_skills/get_skill reach them directly.

tool.name: execute_capability
tool.title: Execute capability
tool.description: Call a capability found via search_capabilities, by its exact name. Pass path/query/body only as described by that match's pathParams/queryParams/hasBody. For external MCP capabilities, provider-advertised schema mismatches are returned as advisory schemaGuidance alongside the provider result; they do not block the downstream call. When the exact capability is a standard MCP App launch tool, this call preserves its originating tool and ui:// binding so compatible OpenWork hosts render it without requiring a generated direct-tool name. For skill capabilities listed in the remote skill catalog, this returns their authorized SKILL.md content; get_skill reads the same content by skill name without a search. Returns the capability's content and, when supplied, its structuredContent unchanged: provider fields, Workflow results, skill content, or an App launch reference. Connection failures can include a connectionAction card; schemaGuidance is advisory. Other failures return error details in text with isError. Returns unknown_capability for stale names; search again.

tool.name: list_skills
tool.title: List skills
tool.description: List every skill available to the signed-in OpenWork member: the built-in Cloud skills plus each marketplace or plugin skill they may use. Read-only; requires an active OpenWork membership. Returns skills (authorized matching descriptors, without SKILL.md content), total (matches before limit), and an optional hint for empty or truncated results. Needs no keywords. Each entry carries the stable name, the exact capability, the title and description, and the marketplace / plugin source when known. Pass the returned name or capability to get_skill to read that skill's SKILL.md. Use query only to narrow a long catalog.

tool.title: Get skill
tool.description: Read one skill's authorized SKILL.md by its name or exact capability, as returned by list_skills or the skill index. Read-only; requires an active OpenWork membership and access to the skill. The text response is the complete SKILL.md; read it fully before following it. Structured content returns the skill descriptor plus content (the complete normalized SKILL.md) and optional provenance; it does not execute the instructions. Returns unknown_skill for missing or ambiguous references, skill_unavailable if the source is gone, or skill_needs_setup with status and action when a required connection is not ready. Call list_skills for an exact name or capability.

tool.name: create_skill
tool.title: Create skill
tool.description: Create one private OpenWork Cloud skill in a new Plugin. Requires an active OpenWork Cloud membership, mcp:write scope, and permission to create Plugins and config objects. Pass a complete SKILL.md with valid name and description frontmatter and instructions. Creates persistent Plugin and skill records, not a draft; the skill is immediately available to its creator. This does not publish it to a Marketplace or share it. Returns structured saved-skill details: schemaVersion, optional mode (omitted means created), name, description, pluginId, skillId, and libraryUrl (or null), plus a text confirmation. Failures return an error code and message with isError.

tool.name: update_skill
tool.title: Update skill
tool.description: Publish a new immutable version of an existing OpenWork Cloud skill, without creating a duplicate Plugin or changing its sharing grants. Requires an active OpenWork Cloud membership, mcp:write scope, and editor access to the skill. Pass its config object id and the complete replacement SKILL.md, not a patch. Immediately replaces the latest instructions for users with access and may remove stale required-connection bindings. Earlier immutable versions remain in history; this tool cannot overwrite or erase a published version. To undo the content change, publish another version with the previous content. Repeated calls create additional versions. Returns structured saved-skill details: schemaVersion, mode (updated), name, description, pluginId (a visible associated Plugin), skillId, and libraryUrl (or null), plus a text confirmation. Failures return an error code and message with isError; a failure resolving saved details can occur after the version was written.

tool.name: render_workflow_artifact
tool.title: View Workflow result
tool.description: Read a retained, successful immutable result from a Workflow the current member can access and display it as an artifact. Use the latest successful snapshot by default, or pass receiptId to select an exact snapshot from that Workflow. Returns structured schemaVersion, artifact metadata (freshness, generation time, Workflow version, receipt and digest), and data, with the retained result as Markdown text for clients without MCP Apps support. Missing, inaccessible, or unreadable snapshots return isError with error and message in JSON text. This tool never runs or refreshes a Workflow, writes a snapshot, or contacts connected providers; use an explicit Workflow run or Automation to refresh data.

maxAgeMs.description: Age threshold in milliseconds for labeling a retained artifact as fresh or stale. Does not filter snapshots, reject stale results, or trigger a refresh.

receiptId.description: An immutable successful run receipt belonging to this Workflow. Omit to read its latest successful retained snapshot; supply to pin an exact historical result.

configObjectId.description: The saved Workflow's configObjectId from capability discovery or a Workflow run, not its Plugin ID, version ID, or artifact view ID. The current member must have access.

outputSchema.description: Retained Workflow artifact: schemaVersion, artifact metadata with freshness and immutable receipt lineage, and original result data. Markdown text accompanies the structured output.

tool.name: execute_capability_script
tool.title: Execute capability script
tool.description: Test a confined JavaScript function body; end with return of JSON-safe data. No imports, fetch, process or host access; use tools for external work and Promise.all for independent calls. mode defaults to adhoc with optional input parameters. Explicit live mode can call the same tools as adhoc (including connection tools), rejects all caller input, and supplies only input.runtime.{now,today,dayStart,dayEnd,timeZone} from the server; optional IANA timeZone defaults to UTC and is live-only. Use exact scriptPath from search_capabilities, never guessed namespaces or operation names. For a discovered Den/native path call it with {path:{...},query:{...},body:{...}} only as advertised; native query parameters must be wrapped in query, e.g. {query:{q:input.query}}. External MCP paths take their argumentsSchema object directly. Example adhoc code: return 1 + 1. Example live code: return {today:input.runtime.today}. tools.$codemode.search({query}) is for adhoc exploration; saved Workflows must call discovered paths directly. Optional inputSchema is checked before dispatch and outputSchema after execution; inspect discovered outputSchema rather than guessing. Returns value and metadata: receiptId, mode, executionType, verification, executedAt/fetchedAt, optional timeZone, and retention (scope, ttlMs, available, canSaveByReceipt, and any error/message). Retention determines whether saveWorkflow can reuse the receipt. This is an authoring test, not a saved Workflow artifact snapshot. To back an App with a reusable live procedure: test with mode:live and outputSchema, saveWorkflow with receiptId and the same schemas (omit code/currentInput), then bind that saved Workflow in create_app with mode live.

_published_faq.name: How do I add OpenWork Connect to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add OpenWork Connect to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.openworklabs.com/mcp/agent.

_published_faq.name: Is OpenWork Connect MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, OpenWork Connect scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is OpenWork Connect's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, OpenWork Connect scores 92/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 14 of 14 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to OpenWork Connect?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to OpenWork Connect in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and Celesto Cloud Computers.
